Rarity.rationale: Obtainable: Common in the transcribed shared grab bag (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pool reports bag=Common).

HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches PotionBelt.cs:15, and it is load-bearing here in a way it is not for the batch's Ancient relics: Potion Belt is COMMON, so without this flag Relic.is_tradable would return True and a spent Potion Belt would be offerable to the trade events. The flag is the only thing stopping that, and the port has it.

AfterObtained.maps_to: no counterpart. `Relic.after_obtained(run)` exists (relics/base.py:138-141) and RunState.add_relic dispatches it (run.py:552); potion_belt.py implements nothing
AfterObtained.rationale: Rollup of guard N1 per binding rule 4. PotionBelt.cs:19-22 is a single `PlayerCmd.GainMaxPotionCount(2, Owner)` and the port drops it, so the sim's belt stays at 3 slots where the game's grows to 5 -- EXECUTED (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b12.py b12-potionbelt): max_potions 3 -> 3 with the relic, against 3 -> 4 for phial_holster and 3 -> 7 for alchemical_coffer, both of which call the helper this relic needs. Waived, not filed as a gap, because the divergent observable is potion-belt CAPACITY and nothing else, and the shared contract puts potions out of scope everywhere ('potions (deferred by Perry)'). Same mechanism and same verdict as relic/alchemical_coffer's AfterObtained and relic/phial_holster N1, both of which waived GainMaxPotionCount on that basis (binding rule 3). See guard N1 for the stub-premise finding and N2 for the exact re-audit instruction.

guards.what: N1 (Sweep C, premise FALSE): the stub's docstring calls this 'an out-of-combat capacity change, so this is a no-op stub' -- the sim has both the hook and the verb, and a sibling relic uses them
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 12 says check the premise rather than accept it, and this one is false in both halves: Relic.after_obtained is a real hook dispatched by RunState.add_relic for every relic in the run (run.py:552), and RunState.add_potion_slots (run.py:492-498) is a direct port of Player.cs's SetMaxPotionCountInternal grow path. phial_holster.py:18 calls exactly that helper for exactly this C# call. So the reason the relic does nothing is not that the sim cannot express it -- it is a one-line omission. Recorded so that Sweep C's headline ('every stub premise the sweep could test is false'; .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md lists potion_belt under the after_obtained family) is confirmed here rather than left implicit. The VERDICT is still waiver and not gap, and the distinction matters: binding rule 1 forbids waiving on 'the sim has no such system', and this waiver does not rest on that -- it rests on the contract's explicit, standing potion exclusion, the same ground relic/alchemical_coffer used for the identical C# verb. NOTE per binding rule 7: relics/base.py, run.py, phial_holster.py, content-relic-sweeps.md and alchemical_coffer.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: what a potion-scope re-audit must check, and the one second-order path by which belt capacity can reach a COMBAT observable
guards.rationale: Stated explicitly so the waiver is re-openable rather than a dead end. (a) The fix is `def after_obtained(self, run): run.add_potion_slots(self.POTION_SLOTS)` with POTION_SLOTS = 2 from DynamicVar('PotionSlots', 2m) (PotionBelt.cs:17) -- the pinned non-ascension value, no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file. (b) It needs undo_after_obtained too (relics/base.py:143-150 exists precisely for pickup effects that mutate run state outside run.relics, so the conformance runner can swap a granted relic back out) -- otherwise a runner swap leaves the extra slots behind, the same class of leak relic/big_mushroom's +20 Max HP produced. (c) The second-order path: belt capacity decides whether a procure SUCCEEDS, since both Player.AddPotionInternal and RunState.add_potion fail silently on a full belt, and relic/belt_buckle's Dexterity turns on whether the belt is EMPTY -- but not on whether it is full, so a missing slot cannot change Belt Buckle's 2 Dexterity by itself. I could not construct a ported chain from the missing slots to a combat number and I am NOT claiming one; the nearest exposure is that a full belt drops relic/petrified_toad's per-combat rock, which changes the potion belt and nothing else. Recorded as an executed negative rather than left as an assumption (binding rule 5). NOTE per binding rule 7: relics/base.py, run.py, player.py, belt_buckle.json, big_mushroom.json and petrified_toad.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: the relic overrides nothing else at all -- no combat hook is hiding in it
guards.rationale: PotionBelt.cs is 23 lines and overrides exactly Rarity, HasUponPickupEffect, CanonicalVars and AfterObtained. There is no combat behaviour, no counter and no ascension branch, so accepting the thin port costs nothing beyond the one waived call -- which is the check the relic-stream brief asks for before a stub is accepted. Confirmed against the harness's own hook enumeration for this unit, which lists exactly those three non-declarative members.
